answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns. A courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use; it is only the courtship event.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; ‘Courtship is an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: move Quarters servants to Available, then Expended servants to Quarters (one space each); resolve the round event, then applicable monument/Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity tile; play exactly the required gentry; provide each required service; resolve all positive favours before negative ones; optionally buy; clear the board. At cleanup used servants go to Expended Service, gentry to personal discard, and the tile returns to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player advances the round marker.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure / Hosting: ordered steps 1–8; ‘only the last player in turn order advances the round marker one space.’

answers.answer: Pass order: servants directly to Available Service; gentry in discard to hand; resolve round-track event, then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; the last player advances the marker. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.’

answers.answer: Yes. Screening uses reputation at the fixed check at the end of step 2, so the 6.1 reputation qualifies PR6 tile and guests. It remains the screening level for the activity even though four Service Help actions reduce actual reputation to 3.4. Each Service Help moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is ‘fixed at the end of step 2’; later special-action losses do not invalidate the activity. Service Help moves one Quarters servant to Available, not from Expended.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; within those groups their order is otherwise chosen. At minimum reputation you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to shelter from its loss; reputation cannot fall below 1.1. A guest with a money penalty requires that penalty be fully payable, using positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money if necessary; if unable to fund it, the guest cannot be played.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6; ‘A money penalty must be fully payable’; ‘You cannot take a negative favour first to shelter it at minimum reputation.’

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gains £100; repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments per servant and moves one servant from Quarters to Available; repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and fully refreshes the Market; this special action is once per turn. At minimum reputation (1.1), you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot move a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and minimum rule: ‘At minimum you cannot ... take a special action’; Service Help ‘cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.’

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room as a Servant Hiring activity, staff it with an available butler or underbutler, and invite no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire (excluding underbutlers) into Expended Service, with no money fee. The upgraded room instead lets you recruit one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; it cannot recruit unique servants.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Room: ‘no gentry’; take up to two from supply into Expended Service; upgraded room recruits one common servant from an opponent’s board.

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With Brushing Room, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even when that servant type remains available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution conditions stated for housekeeper, footmen with Brushing Room, and underbutler.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; take one from supply immediately into Expended Service. Normally it moves to Quarters at your next service rotation, then to Available at your second subsequent rotation; passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier, and Quarters abilities can help once it is there. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Pantry: ‘only way to acquire an underbutler’; it is ‘not immediately available’; ‘An opponent can never recruit your underbutler.’

answers.answer: Market price is the space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You cannot acquire a duplicate of a tile you own. Reputation does not restrict purchase, so you may buy a tile above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: ‘Pay the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve base price is £300’; ‘cannot fall below £100’; reputation does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on the matching Market tile and another tile is drawn. Tiles eligible for Reserve go directly to Reserve and another is drawn. If multiple spaces are being filled, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves that space occupied, so it does not trigger refill.
answers.evidence: Refill paragraph: slide, stack duplicate and draw again, Reserve qualifying tiles draw again, sort only new tiles; one from a stack leaves occupied space.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and send later PR1 draws there too. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. A full Market refresh is standard after each of the first three courtships, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve and Refresh sections state the season 1 and 2 movements and standard refresh after courtships 1–3.

answers.answer: At each courtship both Fairchilds first return to Alderley Hall. For courtships 1–3 score the current face-up theme category, including negative values; the highest gets a VP card and chooses one Fairchild. On a tie, each tied player draws a VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Everyone discards one secret objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together, then bottom-deck them. After seasons 1–3 the first-player marker passes anticlockwise.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep: Fairchild return, theme scoring, tie result, objective discard and anticlockwise marker.

answers.answer: At final courtship score all four revealed theme cards, counting a category repeatedly if repeated (including negative VP). Highest receives one VP card and a Fairchild. Tie is broken by highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied players draw VP cards under the tie rule. Discard the final objective, then players may use special actions and VP-card benefits where possible before Wedding Bells and scoring.
answers.evidence: Final courtship: all four themes, reputation-level tiebreak, final objective discard and final chance to use special actions/VP cards.

answers.answer: Final VP sources: improvement tiles (face-up printed VP, including negatives); gentry in hand and discard (including family, negative VP and final Fairchild); fulfilled objectives; reputation level 1–7 scores 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; 2 VP per servant; wealth 1 VP per £200 rounded down; retained unused VP cards’ printed VP. Highest total wins; ties go to the player with final Fairchild, then highest reputation level; remaining tie is shared. Wheel position has no effect.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and closing tiebreak rules.

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup plus two on round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Extra objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase the retained final total without extra discard. Shuffle simultaneous discards together before bottom-decking. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end; they need not be upgraded.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: five plus two, discard one at each of four courtships, simultaneous discard handling, tile ownership not upgrading.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your own later turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it for its benefit; used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; you cannot receive both benefit and VP from one card.
answers.evidence: VP card rules specify use timing, bottom-of-deck destination, retained scoring and mutually exclusive benefit/VP.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must upgrade/flip to its rose side after first use; a normal already-upgraded tile remains on that side after later uses. Hybrids start with underlined category showing and flip after every use, counting only their currently face-up category for courtship and objectives. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite host once, upgrade into ongoing monuments, and cannot host again. A monument retains its printed tile category and counts for both that category objective and monument objective.
answers.evidence: Improvements: mandatory first-use upgrade and hybrid flip/category; monument section says Queen’s/Lionheart become monuments; objective text says monuments retain category and count for both.

answers.answer: Monuments give one reputation during the ongoing-effects step on each ordinary hosting or passing turn, but not during courtship; a newly bought monument begins on a later turn. Servants’ Hall can be used at the ongoing-effects step on hosting or pass: place any one available servant there to reduce one opponent by one reputation and gain one yourself; that servant goes to Expended at turn end and cannot serve the activity. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects specify monument timing and Servants’ Hall effect, servant destination, and minimum-reputation restriction.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one footman on the tile and one casual guest from hand, with the guest’s normal service; double all guest favours, including negative; it upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses a housekeeper and one prestige guest from hand with normal guest service; double one chosen favour and resolve others normally; it upgrades to a monument. Lionheart Suite uses a butler and draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend, needing no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, excluding negatives from doubling; keep that guest in your discard at cleanup; it upgrades to a monument. Each has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and following fixed-count rule.

answers.answer: Choose a random first player. Starting with the player to that player’s left and going clockwise, each chooses an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith adds its Dowager Countess; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Set the common reputation wheel baseline at 1.1; after family bonus Cavendish starts at 1.4 and Asquith, Ponsonby, and York at 1.1. Use the 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at bottom; no 7/8 counters. Each player gets a butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green with starter side showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–5 give counters, starters, family cards and family bonuses.

answers.answer: For three players, Servants for Hire receives three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers are included. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable for the game.
answers.evidence: Setup: one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; no butlers/housekeepers; unused returned to box.

answers.answer: Shuffle starter guests separately from casual deck and deal two to each player. Shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules; they are not a separate guest type during play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4 and Gentry section: starter guests are casual guests with starter icon.

answers.answer: For four players select five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one). Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze, so both Estate monuments cannot be selected. Selected monuments and all nonstarter base improvement tiles go in the bag; tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against the selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Fill six different eligible Market spaces: PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set aside ineligible draws until all spaces are filled, then return them to the bag. Stack duplicate eligible tiles in the same space. Normal tiles start with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort spaces by ascending sorting number from the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8 gives eligibility, six spaces, handling, orientation and sorting.

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately. Reveal the first theme and leave it face up; keep revealed themes in order through the game. Put base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild cards face up on Alderley Hall. The first theme is open, not hidden, and old revealed themes stay in order rather than leaving play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9: reveal first theme (open courtship), keep revealed themes in order; place Fairchild cards face up.

answers.answer: At hosting-turn rotation, the servant in Quarters moves first to Available; the servant in Expended then moves to Quarters. Each advances exactly one space, so the Expended servant does not move twice. An unused Available servant remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: Quarters to Available first, then Expended to Quarters; unused available servants remain available.

answers.answer: No. The event resolves before choosing/hosting the activity, so a Private Study upgraded later in the same turn does not qualify for that Village Fair reward. An already-upgraded Study earns £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9 only.
answers.evidence: Round-track event resolves before ongoing effects; Village Fair gives £300 and 2 reputation only if Study already upgraded at that step.

answers.answer: Resolve Draw Objectives as the round-track event before ongoing tile effects (after service rotation on a hosting turn, after return of servants and discarded gentry on a pass). Draw two objectives and keep both secret with the others. Passing players receive the event too because events resolve on every player’s turn, including passing.
answers.evidence: Round-track events resolve during hosting and passing; space 6 says draw two and keep both secret.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday ignores PR on all tiles and guests when hosting. All other requirements remain, including service and exact gentry counts/types.
answers.evidence: Round 14 table and hosting rule: ignore PR, still obey all other requirements including service and gentry counts/types.

answers.answer: Yes. On Builders’ Holiday you may buy any number from current Market and/or Reserve within funds. Complete all purchases before sliding/refilling; each tile uses its existing Market-space (or Reserve) price plus modifier, so no sliding changes prices during the sequence. Do not refresh between purchases, including by special action or VP card. Refill all resulting empty spaces together. Market Purchase VP card follows these same Builders’ Holiday rules.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while drawing replacements; refill the six Market spaces under normal rules, then return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix them in. They cannot reappear in that refresh. Reserve remains unchanged.
answers.evidence: Refresh: set all Market tiles aside; refill; then return set-aside tiles to bag; leave Reserve unchanged.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment; move clockwise to gain and anticlockwise to lose. Crossing position 5 to 1 raises a level; crossing 1 to 5 lowers one. Standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum 7.5 (Max.5); losses below minimum are ignored. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; you can take special actions before or during resolving a reputation favour to create space.
answers.evidence: Reputation rules give increment arithmetic, boundaries, min/max, ignoring below-minimum losses, and spending excess at Max.5.

answers.answer: Money is public, not secret. Players may not give or receive money between them in this mode. Never spend more than you have. The supply is unlimited; use proxies if it runs out.
answers.evidence: Money held is public; no player-to-player transfers; never spend more than held; supply unlimited.

answers.answer: Family members can fill a ladies requirement if female, or gentlemen if male, but cannot fill a casual-guest requirement; casual/prestige requirements require that guest type and exclude family. You must play exactly the printed count, with no extra gentry. Family needs no personal service and family cards have no PR.
answers.evidence: Hosting: ladies/gentlemen include matching-gender family; casual/prestige requires guest type and excludes family; exact count; family requires no service and has no PR.

answers.answer: An ordinary guest-invite favour draws a new guest from its indicated deck, reveals it to everyone, and adds it to hand; the printed attendee invite is not played from hand. A screening invite draws the stated number, selects the stated number to keep, reveals only kept cards and adds them to hand. Put rejected screened cards on the bottom of their guest deck without revealing them.
answers.evidence: Gentry invite definitions and screening paragraph.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so you need not dismiss if you do not want to. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity or discard, including one drawn earlier in the same favour resolution; family cannot be dismissed. Put the guest on bottom of its matching deck: it is no longer yours, will not return on passing, and scores no VP.
answers.evidence: Dismissal is ‘always optional’; eligible zones and guest just drawn; family exception and ownership/scoring consequences stated.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose screening two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lord has no choice; Lady and Heir offer choices; Dowager gives both.
answers.evidence: Base family card table.

answers.answer: Young Lady gains the two-reputation admirer bonus when attending with a male prestige guest, including Charles Fairchild. A male casual guest does not qualify; a female prestige guest does not qualify. She always draws one casual guest as her normal favour, with the two reputation additionally when the condition is met.
answers.evidence: Young Lady table: draw one casual; bonus if male prestige guest attends. Charles is explicitly male prestige and triggers it.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest, no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest, no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives one prestige guest plus two reputation. Both are guests, not family, so neither has family dismissal immunity and both can be dismissed normally.
answers.evidence: Gentry section states Fairchild genders/type/service/favours/PR and that neither has family dismissal immunity.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent by one reputation. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one reputation. A player at minimum reputation cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gentry section lists both gossip effects; reputation rule protects a player at minimum from opponent reductions.

answers.answer: Barn gives one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. It gives none just for owning an Estate tile or when passing.
answers.evidence: Barn: ‘every time you host an Estate activity, gain one reputation’; no reputation for owning or passing.

answers.answer: Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available and all Expended servants to Quarters, one space each, at hosting-turn start, without reputation cost. Servants’ Quarters improvement lets you use one servant still in Quarters after rotation in addition to Available, without reputation cost; that servant goes to Expended at turn end. Service Help costs 3 increments to move one Quarters servant to Available and can repeat; it cannot take directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Service mechanism table compares ordinary rotation, Servants’ Quarters, and Service Help.

answers.answer: Front-side Private Study requires two family and a butler, with no tile favour. It upgrades permanently to an ongoing tile; once upgraded it is not hosted again. It gives £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair rounds only, so you cannot repeatedly host it for that income.
answers.evidence: Private Study rule explicitly states two family, butler, no favour, upgrades to ongoing effect and pays only on Village Fair.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library uses a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library uses a butler and three family and draws one VP card. Extra objectives increase the number retained for final scoring and do not cause an extra courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Main Library paragraph and objective rule on extra objectives.

answers.answer: Objective VP-card benefit draws two objectives, keeps one, and returns the other to the bottom of the objective deck. It adds one additional retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Objective draws two, keep one, return other to bottom; gives one additional retained objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service, including those in Expended, and they can be used immediately. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves only one servant from Quarters to Available; it cannot move directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table contrasts Refresh Service and Service Help.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutler, into Expended Service. Since it enters Expended, it cannot immediately provide service; it must advance through rotation unless another rule changes its location.
answers.evidence: Hire Servant benefit: take one from supply, not underbutler, into Expended Service; ordinary rotation advances it one space.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest may return one gentry including a family member from personal discard to hand. If returned before Invite Gentry, you may then choose that card to attend this activity, subject to normal requirements; it is not automatically played.
answers.evidence: Refresh Guest VP benefit explicitly includes family and explains use before Invite Gentry.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets and lady’s maids, excluding butler, housekeeper and underbutler. Ordinary service VP instead gives 2 VP for every servant of any type. The ten-servant objective awards 7 VP for at least ten servants total, all servant types.
answers.evidence: Objective section explicitly restricts basic servants; final VP counts all servants; servant-set objective says ten servants total.

answers.answer: Both upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite count as monuments for the monument objective and retain their Estate and Prestige categories, respectively, for category objectives. A hybrid counts only in its currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Objective note explicitly names Queen’s Suite as Estate and Lionheart as Prestige and counts each for monument; hybrids count face-up category.

answers.answer: Nature Group is worth 11 VP and requires Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is worth 12 VP and requires Gabled Conservatory plus one of Main Library or North Library. The tiles need only be owned at game end; use or upgrading is unnecessary.
answers.evidence: Group objective list and objective rule: owning tiles suffices; use/upgrading unnecessary.

answers.answer: Prestige-guest objective scores 1 VP per prestige guest. Every-three-guests counts all nonfamily guests; only each complete set of three scores, so an incomplete group earns no point. A final Fairchild is a prestige guest and counts as a nonfamily guest.
answers.evidence: Objective table gives 1 VP per prestige guest or per complete three nonfamily guests; guest rules include final Fairchild as prestige guest.

answers.answer: The reputation objective awards 7 VP for reaching maximum level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective awards 10 VP for at least £1200. Wheel position does not affect ordinary reputation VP or reputation tie resolution; final scoring uses level and wheel position never breaks a tie.
answers.evidence: Objective table and final VP/courtship tiebreak text state level 7, £1200, and wheel position has no effect.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family cards. Unupgraded favour: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded favour: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity or discard to the bottoms of their appropriate decks. It remains an activity on both sides and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: West Terrace paragraph states same service/count on both sides, favours, optional dismissal, and no ongoing tile.

answers.answer: There is no hand or discard-pile limit. Gentry in your discard pile still belong to you and score normally; passing recovers them to hand.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: ‘There is no hand or discard-pile limit’; discard gentry score normally and passing recovers them.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one, including one beneath another in a stack; there is no top-tile-only restriction. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve: ‘Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection. You may inspect all tiles at any time and buy any one ... including a tile underneath another in a stack.’

answers.answer: You may choose to pass even if you can host. If the preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says choose host or pass; hosting step 5 says choose another legal activity or pass, and if none possible you must pass.

answers.answer: Yes. On a passing turn you may take the free passing-benefit refresh, also use one paid special-action Market refresh (cost 4 reputation increments), and use multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each for a separate full refresh. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the paid special-action refresh; free passing and VP-card refreshes are separate.
answers.evidence: Special actions: other refresh methods do not use the allowance; multiple Market Refresh VP cards may be used and may combine with free pass and paid refresh.

answers.answer: No interrupt actions are allowed while another player takes a turn. Special actions may be taken at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing, with sufficient reputation to pay.
answers.evidence: Special actions are available ‘at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing.’

answers.answer: No. Favours are mandatory unless expressly optional, so you cannot decline an ordinary printed guest invite while taking the other favours. An optional dismissal favour may be declined; if used, dismissal is optional and you choose an eligible guest to put on the bottom of its matching deck.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6 says favours are mandatory unless expressly optional; dismissal section says dismissal is always optional.
